summary: Stage 1 of 2: tensor-level, model-independent prediction and decision modules under src/cam_live/predict (dists, world, imagination, errors, evaluator, calibration, policy, voi, registry, candidates), 120 tests (119 CPU default, 1 gpu-marked). All requirements are 'partial': modules implemented and tested on synthetic ground truth and LabWorld; wiring onto the real model and the agent is stage 2.

PI-01.limitations: Stage 1 (tensor-level, synthetic ground truth and the LabWorld diagnostic). Not yet wired onto CamLiveModel / the agent: no LossProvider, heads not registered on the model, nothing under runtime/ imports cam_live.predict. z comes from a synthetic projection in tests, not from the experiential core. World output is not yet combined with A's Bayesian fast layer.

Not yet wired onto CamLiveModel / the agent: no LossProvider, heads not registered on the model, nothing under runtime/ imports cam_live.predict. Single writer process per registry file. PredictionRecord has no registered_at field (change request B-CR-3); the registry keeps it.

not_done: Stage 2 wiring is not done: no learning_api.LossProvider objects for world / evaluator / transition / downstream losses; heads are not registered on CamLiveModel; nothing in the runtime or agent imports cam_live.predict.
No test runs against Workstream A's real model (backbone, experiential core, decision_latent, features); every z / b in the tests is synthetic or a fixed projection of exact LabWorld quantities.
World-model output is not combined with A's Bayesian fast layer; VOI is not connected to the model's feature map phi or FastBeliefState (voi_sampling takes them as callables).
Backbone candidate generation is not exercised: no generate() call; parse_actions is tested on written JSON only.
Choosing which experiment to run (hypothesis formation from uncertainty) is not implemented here; the registry records, randomises, matures and analyses experiments.
Imagination is validated on synthetic latent dynamics only; HorizonController is not yet fed by real replay; imagine_candidates is single-step.
No dedicated evaluator head for sustainability / other future outcomes (spec 6.2): they must be asked as world-model queries.
Exploration rules are implemented with exact propensities but not yet compared with each other on a task (spec 5.1 'initially compare').
Error-source attribution is rule-based; 'incorrect causal assumptions' is not separated from other confident misses (label model_wrong).
JSON-Schema support is a subset ($ref, if/then/else, patternProperties, dependent*, format unchecked).
Registries are single-writer: the in-memory index is not refreshed if another process appends to the same file.
No change was made to master-owned contracts; 5 change requests are open in docs/change_requests/B.md (PROGRAM_OPERATION currently lives in predict/candidates.py).
scientific_failures: The learned DownstreamValueEstimator did not beat an accurate computed VOI on held-out probes (Spearman 0.617 vs 0.671; learned_beats_reference=False). It only beat a deliberately mis-specified reference (-0.335). The computed VOI stays the reference.

Poisson-GLM VOI with the assumed-density update over-estimates the realised gain in magnitude (computed [0.55, 0.137, 0.0] vs realised [0.376, 0.103, 0.0]); the ranking of probes is correct and the irrelevant probe is exactly 0. Bernoulli: computed [0.0339, 0.0063, 0.0] vs realised [0.0327, 0.0104, 0.0].
After training, the evaluator is still mildly over-confident on held-out trajectories: calibration slope 0.69 (1.0 = calibrated), ECE 0.068 (from 0.477).

A plain bootstrapped ensemble (prior_scale=0) did not reliably report higher epistemic uncertainty off-distribution (off/in ratio below 1 in 2 of 12 runs, minimum 0.61); randomised prior functions are therefore on by default (minimum ratio 2.57 over 12 runs).

At random initialisation the policy's dependence on the belief is weak in absolute terms (KL 2.6e-04 under belief permutation; all logits are near zero by the small-init design). It is 15.7 after training on a belief-dependent task.

Decision-blind information gain is a fairly good proxy in the random linear-Gaussian bandit family (Spearman 0.85 vs 0.97 for VOI and -0.23 for raw surprise): the family does not separate VOI from information gain as sharply as the noisy-TV case does.
